The unemployment rate is 9.6%, fed funds is about 0.2%, and core CPI is 0.59% YoY. That pattern fits late 2010. Core CPI hit about 0.6% in October 2010, and the unemployment rate was 9.6% in September 2010 and 9.8% in November.

The 10-year yield at 2.84% with a 3-month change of +0.37 points to October 2010 (it was about 2.5% in October and 2.8% at the end of November). The 1-month equity return of 0.0% and the 3-month return of +13.1% fit November 2010: the S&P 500 was roughly flat that month, and it was up strongly from August. Developed ex-US equity fell 4.8% in November on the European debt crisis, which also fits. VIX at 21.5 matches end of November. Unemployment is probably the 9.8% reading in November, but the snapshot shows 9.6%, which could reflect publication timing or a different vintage. The 10-year yield was 2.8% at end of November, so I'm going with November 2010.
